positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, validation among them, overrides the prototype default.
No error is shown for a missing, badly formed or out-of-range arrival date; it only affects completeness.
No error is shown for a missing or unrecognised port of entry.
Transport identification has no format or length check.
Transport document reference has no format or length check.
The server does not check that a transit country is on the list or not repeated.
When the means of transport error shows, everything else entered is still saved.
An arrival date that is not a real date is refused with 'Enter a real arrival date'.
A port not in the list is refused with 'Select a valid option'.
Transport identification over 58 characters is refused.
Adding a country already in the list is refused by name.
At most 12 transit countries can be listed on a notification.
When the arrival date is out of window nothing on the page is saved.
Transport identification and transport document reference each have a place for an error message, but no validation ever sets one.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and names validation as a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real service keeps every server-side field check and its message: the real-date and window checks on the arrival date, the stale-date and stale-port flags, the in-list checks on port and means of transport (the stale saved means of transport included), the 58-character limits, and the transit checks (nothing chosen, not on the list, already added, the 12-country cap, stale saved countries). A page with any error saves nothing and shows the entries back. Where Design Release 2.1 does validate, means of transport required on Save and continue, it is adopted. The prototype's soft-validation claims are set aside.
